chapters.title: Introduction
intro: This chapter is for everyone. It explains what SupportDesk does, which part of it you use, and the ideas you meet in every chapter.
Read it first. Then go to the chapters for your role.

sections.title: What SupportDesk does
intro: SupportDesk is a help desk. It collects customer questions from e-mail, the customer portal, live chat, messaging apps and phone calls in one place.
Each question becomes a ticket. Agents answer tickets, and timers show how much time is left to respond. Customers follow their tickets in the portal or the mobile app.

SupportDesk also keeps your customers, their products and their contracts. It has a knowledge base of help articles and reports on how the team performs. An AI assistant can summarise tickets and draft replies for you to check.

sections.title: Who uses which part
sections.intro: SupportDesk has several apps. You use only the ones your role needs.

rows: Answer tickets and chats, look up customers, use the knowledge base, see your work and the team's work.
Set up the workspace: users and roles, channels, SLA policies, automation, brands, security and billing.
Raise and follow tickets, read help articles, ask the community and chat with support.
Work on tickets or follow your own tickets from a phone, even with a weak connection.
Run the SupportDesk service: workspaces, plans, invoices and support access.

blocks.note: You see only the menus and buttons your role allows. If a task in this manual names a menu you cannot see, ask your administrator for access.

sections.title: The desk at a glance
sections.intro: The desk opens after you sign in. The same frame surrounds every page: the menu on the left and the top bar above the page.

blocks.caption: The desk with the **Command Center** page open.
blocks.alt: SupportDesk desk with the navigation menu, top bar and the Command Center page, with numbered highlights

callouts: The **navigation menu** opens each part of the desk. It is grouped into **Work**, **Customers**, **Operations** and **Settings**.
**Search** finds tickets and opens pages and commands. Press [[Ctrl+K]] to open it from anywhere.
**New ticket** creates a ticket for a customer.
The **notifications** bell shows how many notifications you have not read.
**Availability** tells your team whether you can take new work, for example **Online** or **Away**.
Your **account menu** holds your profile, your preferences and **Sign out**.
The **page header** shows the page title and its main buttons.

blocks.tip: Select **Collapse** at the bottom of the menu to show icons only. This gives the page more room.

sections.title: Key ideas
sections.intro: These words appear throughout the manual. The glossary at the end explains more of them.

rows: One customer question or problem, with every message, note and change about it. Each ticket has a number, such as **#1004**.
Where a ticket is in its life, such as **Open**, **In Progress** or **Resolved**. Chapter 5 lists every status.
How urgent a ticket is: **Low**, **Medium**, **High** or **Critical**.
The service level agreement. It sets how soon the team must respond to and resolve a ticket. Timers count down on each ticket.
The way a ticket arrives, such as e-mail, the portal, live chat, a messaging app or a phone call.
A saved list of tickets, such as **My open tickets** or **Unassigned**. Agents work from views.
Groups of agents. A ticket belongs to a department, and routing assigns it to a team or an agent.
Your organisation's own SupportDesk. You enter its short name when you sign in.
A company name, logo and portal that customers see. One workspace can serve several brands.
Help articles for agents and customers. Customers read published articles in the portal.

sections.title: How to use this manual
intro: Each chapter starts by saying who it is for. Tasks have numbered steps, and the result tells you what you see when you finish.
The screenshots come from a demonstration workspace. Your workspace has its own names, numbers and settings, so your screens look a little different.

list: New to the desk? Read chapters 2 to 6 first.
Supervisors: read chapters 12, 15 and 16 as well.
Administrators: start with chapter 17, then the chapters for each setting you manage.
Platform operators: go straight to chapter 31.

glossary.definition: A support team member who answers tickets and chats in the desk.
A team lead who watches the queue, SLA risk and the team's workload, and moves work between agents.
A person who sets up the workspace: users, roles, channels, policies, security and billing.
A person at the company that runs the SupportDesk service. Operators manage workspaces, plans and invoices in the platform console.
One customer question or problem, with all its messages, notes and changes. Each ticket has a number.
Service level agreement. The response and resolution times the team promises, measured by timers on each ticket.
A way customers reach you, such as e-mail, the portal, live chat, a messaging app or phone.
Your organisation's own SupportDesk, with its own users, customers and settings. You enter its short name when you sign in.
A company name, logo and customer portal. One workspace can serve several brands.
The website where customers raise and follow tickets, read help articles and chat with support.
The SupportDesk app that agents, supervisors and administrators use in a web browser.
